quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Send and void have no handling for a rejected fetch, and the success path says nothing
evidence: fetch rejects on network failure; there is no try/catch around app.js:26 or app.js:33, so the click handler ends in an unhandled promise rejection and the user sees nothing (the alert at line 27 is only for a non-2xx status). On success app.js:28 only increments sentCount, which nothing displays; the lines stay in the list and the total stays. Void (app.js:34) shows nothing on success either. No Content-Type header is set for the JSON body.
failing_case: Go offline and press "Send invoice": no alert, no message, nothing changes, and the user cannot tell if the invoice went out. On an online success the page looks identical, so the user presses it again (and tooSoon never blocks it) and sends a duplicate. An empty list can also be sent.
remediation: Wrap each call in try/catch, show an inline status region for sending, sent (with a reference), and failed with cause and next step, disable the button while pending, clear or lock the lines after success, and refuse to send an empty invoice.

title: validQuantity accepts empty, blank, zero, negative, fractional, hex and exponent values
evidence: isNaN coerces its argument: isNaN("") and isNaN("  ") are false, isNaN("-3"), "0", "1.5", "1e9", "0x10" and "Infinity" are false. app.js:19 only combines it with price > 0 and app.js:20 stores Number(qtyText). Number("") is 0. The input has inputmode="numeric" only, which does not validate (index.html:16). Traced; the comment says "must be a number" but the invoice needs a positive whole number.
failing_case: Leave Quantity empty with a price of 10 and press Add line: a line of 0 x 10.00 is added. Enter -3 and price 10: the total drops by 30.00 and a credit line is sent as an invoice line. Enter 1e9 or Infinity: total becomes 1e10 or Infinity and toFixed prints "Infinity".
remediation: Validate with a pattern such as /^[1-9]\d{0,5}$/ (or Number.isInteger and a maximum) and put the same rule on the server. Add type/min/step/required on the input too.

title: tooSoon never trips: lastSend is never updated, so double-send protection does nothing
evidence: `lastSend` is declared at guards.js:22 and read here. Grep of both scripts shows no assignment. app.js:28 increments `sentCount` instead, which nothing reads. Date.now() - 0 is always more than 1000, so tooSoon() is always false. Nothing disables #send while the POST is in flight (app.js:24-29).
failing_case: Double-click "Send invoice" (or press Enter twice on the focused button): both clicks pass tooSoon(), two POST /api/invoices requests carry the same lines, and the client is billed twice. A retry after a slow response does the same.
remediation: Set `lastSend = Date.now()` before the fetch, or better disable the button and hold an in-flight flag until the request settles, and send an idempotency key so the server also ignores a repeat.

title: canVoid is inverted: every non-admin may void, an admin listed first may not
evidence: Array.indexOf returns -1 when absent (truthy) and 0 when "admin" is the first element (falsy). The signed-in user in app.js:2 has roles ["viewer","billing"], so indexOf is -1, canVoid returns true, and app.js:32 lets the click go on to POST /api/invoices/void. Traced, not executed (Bash was denied).
failing_case: user.roles = ["viewer","billing"] -> canVoid() is true and the void request is sent. user.roles = ["admin"] -> indexOf is 0, canVoid() is false and the admin cannot void. ["viewer","admin"] -> 1, true. Access is decided by the position in the array.
remediation: Use `user.roles.includes("admin")` and add a test for no role, admin first, admin later. Enforce the same rule on the server for /api/invoices/void, because the browser check alone is not access control.

title: Invoice lines live only in memory and there is no way to remove or edit one
evidence: `lines` is a module variable, never persisted and never mutated except push (app.js:20). There is no remove/edit control in index.html and no beforeunload guard.
failing_case: Enter ten lines, mistype a price on one: the only fix is to reload and lose all ten. A refresh or accidental back navigation also drops the draft with no warning.
remediation: Add a remove and edit control per line, save the draft to localStorage with a version and a guarded load, and warn on unload while there are unsent lines.

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Money is summed in binary floating point inside render code
evidence: The total is computed in the view function with float multiplication and addition, rounded only on display with toFixed(2); the same total is not what is sent (app.js:26 sends raw qty and price). Prices such as 1.005 or 0.1 x 3 accumulate error, and toFixed can round a half cent the wrong way (1.005.toFixed(2) is "1.00").
failing_case: Add a line of qty 3 at price 1.005: the page shows 3.01 or 3.02 depending on the sum order, while rounding each line to cents gives 3.02 (3 x 1.01) or 3.00; the displayed total can differ from the sum of the displayed line amounts and from the server's total.
remediation: Move the pricing into one pure, tested function that works in integer cents (round the unit price to cents on entry), and have the view only display its result. The server remains the authority for the total.

title: Invalid add-line input is rejected silently, with no message and no focus move
evidence: The submit handler returns with no output. The inputs have no aria-invalid, no error text and no required on qty/price (index.html:16, 18); only Client has `required`. Driven in head only: traced.
failing_case: Type "abc" in Quantity or leave Unit price empty and press Add line: nothing happens. A keyboard or screen-reader user gets no hint that the line was refused or which field is wrong. A client of only spaces also passes the browser `required` check but is stored as an empty name (line 16 trims after validation).
remediation: Show a per-field error message linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, move focus to the first bad field, and reject an empty trimmed client.

title: Void invoice is irreversible, has no confirmation, and no affordance for who may use it
evidence: index.html:24 renders the button for every user. The handler posts at once (app.js:33) with no confirm, no pending state and no success message, and the user is hardcoded at app.js:2. A non-admin gets no explanation; combined with the inverted check it works for them.
failing_case: A stray click or Enter on the focused "Void invoice" button, which sits directly beside "Send invoice" with identical styling, sends the void request immediately; the page shows nothing, so the user does not know whether the invoice is void.
remediation: Confirm in a dialog that names the invoice, separate and style the destructive control, disable or hide it for users without the role, and report the result in a status region.

title: escapeHtml does not escape quotes but its output is put inside a double-quoted attribute
evidence: guards.js:5 replaces only &, < and >. app.js:8 places the result in title="..." and assigns the string with innerHTML. Traced: a client of `x" onmouseover="alert(1)" autofocus tabindex="0` gives `title="x" onmouseover="alert(1)" autofocus tabindex="0"`, which is a live event-handler attribute.
failing_case: Type `x" onmouseover="alert(document.domain)" x="` in Client, set quantity 1 and price 1, press Add line. The new <a> carries an onmouseover handler and runs script when hovered. Where the client name comes from a shared source (imported client list, another user), this is stored XSS on an invoice/billing page.
remediation: Escape " and ' too (or build nodes with createElement/textContent and setAttribute, which avoids HTML parsing). Add a test with a quote-bearing name.
fix: not offerable: unbalanced brackets or quotes

title: Each line renders a dead link (href="#") with no action
evidence: The anchor has no handler and no real target. It is keyboard-focusable (a:focus-visible is styled in styles.css:5), so Tab stops once per line on a control that does nothing. Activating it appends # to the URL and scrolls to the top. Its title repeats the link text. Screen readers announce a link with no destination.
failing_case: Add three lines, then Tab through the page: three extra tab stops. Press Enter on one: the page jumps to the top and the URL gains `#`, with no other effect. A user may expect it to open or edit the client.
remediation: Render the client name as plain text. If the link is meant to edit or open the client, give it a real href or make it a button with a handler and a name.
